original_card.question: Can one uncovered interface implication be formalized with exact caller and certificate bindings?
methods: Formalize a missing boundary lemma identified by the selected review.
Audit a formal theorem-to-certificate binding independently.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State the exact formalized proposition and remaining assumptions; avoid duplicate arithmetic formalizations already present.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one missing statement with quantified hypotheses, actual caller and existing coverage. A compact-switch lemma is a candidate only after its mathematical contract is reviewed. Establish a bounded proof plan before a separately budgeted proof-assistant build; do not rerun large Lean jobs as orientation.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A missing interface proof can reduce the conditional gap even if it does not change kappa.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one formal lemma or one theorem-to-certificate binding.
scope_change_triggers: Formalizing already-covered arithmetic and claiming the full multiplication theorem.

existing_checks.remaining: Exact theorem-to-caller binding and genuinely uncovered interface lemmas.
Uniform algorithmic implications, not another endpoint digit.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: compact-switch formalization proposed as future validation.
existing_checks.remaining: Audit the statement and assumptions before a formal proof campaign.

actual_scope: Closed form for the ground-field determinant of an isomorphism between two power-basis presentations of the same finite residue field, for Open next question 2 of apoursh's PR #5663. PR #5668 already computes these determinants numerically; this adds the closed form and its sign rule.
scope_change_reason: The formal-interface card asks for an uncovered interface implication. PR #5663 requires identical residue presentations and states that comparing different ones needs a checked field isomorphism with its determinant. This package supplies that determinant as a written theorem with exhaustive prime-field evidence, not a Lean formalization.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the determinant-character interface; it does not change kappa or any supplier.
stop_rule: Stop after the closed form, its sign rule and the component tensor-power rule are proved and checked; recognizer and caller work are out of scope.
evidence: PROOF in README.md; verify.py exhaustively checks 18,157 ordered presentation pairs and 51,300 isomorphisms over twelve (p,d) domains.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Cross-check the det(Q) field factors computed by PR #5668's linear solves against det(phi_j)^(N_j) from the closed form.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It gives an independent arithmetic check of a numerically computed normalization.
open_questions.first_step: Read each recovered field map's image of the reference generator and evaluate the Vandermonde ratio.
open_questions.blocked_by: Not run here; requires instrumenting the PR #5668 bridge.

open_questions.question: Extend the closed form to non-power bases, such as normal bases, used by a real producer.
open_questions.why_it_matters: A native caller may not store residue fields in power bases.
open_questions.first_step: Write the basis change to the power basis and multiply by its determinant.
open_questions.blocked_by: No named producer or consumer basis is supplied.
